clue.text: A crude waste of paint (glossy)

parts.note: oil is a kind of paint used by artists
slick means smooth and glossy

explanation.surface: A painter complains that a glossy coat of paint was a crude waste of materials.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crude' looks like an adjective about the painting, but it is crude oil, and the spillage is the waste.
explanation.definitionFit: A spill of crude petroleum spreading across the sea is waste floating on the water.

clue.text: Upset by rotten finish

parts.note: food that has gone off is rotten
an end is a finish

explanation.surface: Someone is upset by a rotten finish to a match.
explanation.definitionFit: To affront someone is to hurt their feelings, the verb sense of upset.

clue.text: Access given to the French ambassador

parts.note: le is French for 'the'
a gate gives access to a field or garden

explanation.surface: The French ambassador is granted access.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given to' is only a joining phrase; 'Access' looks like a verb but is a noun, an entrance.
explanation.definitionFit: A legate is a diplomatic envoy, especially one sent by the Pope.

clue.text: The French run the German food supply

parts.note: la is a French word for 'the' (feminine)
R is the cricket abbreviation for a run
der is German for 'the' (masculine)

explanation.surface: French and German partners share out a supply of food.
explanation.definitionFit: A pantry or storeroom holds a household's stock of provisions.

clue.text: Ride to a northern town from a southern city

parts.note: to canter is to ride at a gentle gallop
Bury is a town near Manchester in northern England

explanation.surface: A rider travels on horseback from a city in the south up to a town in the north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' joins the two pieces. Bury is in Greater Manchester; Canterbury is a cathedral city in Kent, south-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: Canterbury, famous for its cathedral, lies in Kent in the south of England.

clue.text: Heading off to sleep — like a log?

indicators.note: the heading, or first letter, of the word for sleep is taken off

parts.note: slumber means sleep

explanation.surface: Someone nods off and sleeps like a log.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sleep like a log' is a set phrase, but here 'like a log' defines timber, and 'Heading off' drops the first letter of SLUMBER.
explanation.definitionFit: Lumber is sawn timber, material of the same kind as a felled tree trunk.

clue.text: Returning letters with no time to be precise

indicators.note: the letters of the word Returning are taken and rearranged
with no means the letter for time is removed

explanation.surface: Letters are sent back without delay so as to be precise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no' removes T (time) from RETURNING, leaving REURNING; 'letters' asks for those letters to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Unerring means never making a mistake, so always exact.

clue.text: Chamber, when full, had this to report

definitions.meaning: the chamber of a gun, when loaded, has a round of ammunition in it
a news report or official statement

explanation.surface: A loaded gun chamber hints at the sound of a gunshot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'report' also suggests a gunshot, but it is a news announcement; the first part reads as two words, a round in the chamber.
explanation.definitionFit: A news bulletin is a short report; a loaded chamber holds a cartridge inside it.

clue.text: Taking stock of road protected by decree

indicators.note: the road's abbreviation is shielded by being placed inside the word for decree

parts.note: a ruling is an official decree
ST is short for street, a road

explanation.surface: A road is protected by decree while the authorities take stock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking stock' looks like reviewing inventory, but it means stealing livestock.
explanation.definitionFit: Rustling is stealing cattle or horses, literally carrying off livestock.

clue.text: Maybe Oscar ordered gunfire to cover unit

indicators.note: the shuffled letters are made to cover, or go around, the letter for one
ordered means arranged into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral one, a unit

explanation.surface: Gunfire is ordered to cover a military unit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' rearranges GUNFIRE to FIGURNE, which 'to cover' puts round I. An Oscar is a statuette, so 'Maybe' marks an example.
explanation.definitionFit: The Academy Award statuette is a small model of a human form, an example of a statuette.

clue.text: Young ladies in ecstasy, wearing rings?

indicators.note: the word for rings wears, or carries around, the letter for ecstasy

parts.note: bells are rings, as on a telephone
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Young ladies in raptures show off their rings.
explanation.definitionFit: Belles are beautiful young women, especially the most admired at a ball.

clue.text: Talked about new leader poorly treated

indicators.note: the leader of the word new is its first letter
poorly signals that the letters of treated are arranged badly

explanation.surface: People gossiped about a new leader who was treated poorly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poorly' is the anagram signal; 'new leader' looks like a fresh boss but just gives the first letter of 'new'.
explanation.definitionFit: To natter is to chat idly, so nattered about means chatted about something.

clue.text: Writer's love-end of winter and spring

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

indicators.note: end of means the last letter of the word winter

parts.note: a well is a spring of water

explanation.surface: A writer's love fades at the end of winter and the start of spring.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', linking the definition: George Orwell wrote 1984 and Animal Farm.
explanation.definitionFit: George Orwell was the pen name of the novelist Eric Blair.

clue.text: Displaying a hatred, yet prepared for action

indicators.note: displaying signals that the letters are laid out afresh in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone shows hatred yet stays ready to fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Displaying' rearranges A HATRED YET.
explanation.definitionFit: A weapon held at the ready is poised for immediate use.

clue.text: Sailors reported stress of not voting

parts.note: ABs are able seamen, ordinary sailors

indicators.note: reported means the word for stress is as heard spoken

parts.note: tension is stress

explanation.surface: Sailors report feeling stressed about not voting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reported' makes TENSION sound like TENTION. The definition 'of not voting' reads as the act of not voting.
explanation.definitionFit: An abstention is a deliberate choice to cast no ballot.

clue.text: Countryman who feels at home on space vehicle?

parts.note: in means at home, as in 'staying in'
a lander is a craft that touches down on a planet or moon

explanation.surface: An astronaut from the country feels at home on a space vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer the first piece sits on top of the second, hence 'on'; 'who feels' only colours the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: An inlander lives in the interior of a country, away from the coast.

clue.text: Custodians and cooks hiding a rugged exterior

indicators.note: the word for cooks hides the other letters inside it

parts.note: to stew is to cook slowly, so cooks gives stews

indicators.note: the exterior of rugged is its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Custodians and cooks hide their rough exteriors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a rugged exterior' looks like a description of the stewards, but gives A plus the outside letters of 'rugged'.
explanation.definitionFit: Stewards look after property or events on someone else's behalf, as caretakers.

clue.text: Sway outside, sick-drinking too much?

indicators.note: the word for sway goes outside the word for sick

parts.note: to swing is to sway
ill means sick

explanation.surface: A drunk sways outside, sick from drinking too much.
explanation.definitionFit: Swilling is gulping drink greedily, as a heavy drinker does.

clue.text: In theory, town planning is of significance

indicators.note: planning signals that the letters are laid out anew

explanation.surface: In theory, town planning matters a great deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'planning' rearranges THEORY TOWN.
explanation.definitionFit: Something worth noting is important, having significance.

clue.text: Maintain course, embraced by skill

indicators.note: embraced by means the course is held inside the word for skill

parts.note: art is skill
SSE, south-south-east, is a compass course

explanation.surface: A craftsman maintains a course of training with skill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'course' is a compass heading, SSE (south-south-east), not a programme of study.
explanation.definitionFit: To assert is to state firmly, to maintain that something is true.

clue.text: This fighter's right to sup port hot property dealer

indicators.note: in a down clue the letter for right supports what sits above it

parts.note: a fence deals in stolen, or hot, goods

explanation.surface: A fighter backs a dealer in stolen goods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hot property' means stolen goods; in a down answer R goes under FENCE.
explanation.definitionFit: A fencer is a swordsman who fights with foil, épée or sabre.

clue.text: Pies have risen -a number of layers

indicators.note: in a down clue risen means the word for pies is read bottom to top

parts.note: tarts are pies

explanation.surface: Pies have risen into a number of layers.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer 'have risen' reads the word upwards, so the pies come out backwards before A.
explanation.definitionFit: Strata are layers of rock or of society, stacked one upon another.

clue.text: A sort of cavalry, if you please!

parts.note: cavalry twill is a strong woven fabric, so twill is a sort of it

explanation.surface: A cavalry officer is invited to choose whatever pleases him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cavalry' suggests horsemen, but cavalry twill is a sturdy cloth used for trousers.
explanation.definitionFit: At will means as one pleases, whenever one wishes.

clue.text: Search for gold exposed by Panorama

definitions.meaning: to explore ground looking for ore or precious metal
a wide view over a landscape

explanation.surface: A gold search is revealed by a television programme.
explanation.walkthrough: Panorama is also a BBC current affairs programme, which suits the surface's 'exposed by'.
explanation.definitionFit: Prospectors look for gold deposits; a prospect is also a sweeping view or vista.

clue.text: A blunder, mistakenly revealing one's skin

indicators.note: revealing means the letters are laid bare inside the words blunder, mistakenly

explanation.surface: A blunder mistakenly exposes someone's skin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mistakenly' looks like an anagram signal but is part of the run.
explanation.definitionFit: The dermis is the thick inner layer of the skin under the epidermis.

clue.text: Roman road crossing awfully clean European city

indicators.note: the Roman road crosses over, so it goes around the other letters

parts.note: via is Latin for road

indicators.note: awfully signals that clean is badly arranged

explanation.surface: A Roman road runs through a very clean European city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awfully' is the anagram signal, not an intensifier on 'clean'. Valencia is in Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: Valencia is a port city on the east coast of Spain.

clue.text: The rule accepts a quarter leave voluntarily

indicators.note: accepts means the word for rule takes the letter in

parts.note: to reign is to rule
S, south, is a quarter of the compass

explanation.surface: Under the rule, a quarter of staff accept and leave voluntarily.
explanation.definitionFit: To resign is to give up a job or office of one's own accord.

clue.text: Externally, heavy satire generates panic attacks

indicators.note: externally means the first and last letters of heavy
generates signals that satire's letters are made into something new

explanation.surface: Heavy satire provokes panic.
explanation.walkthrough: HY (the first and last letters of 'heavy') joins STERIA, the anagram of SATIRE that 'generates' makes.
explanation.definitionFit: Hysteria is uncontrolled emotional excess, seen in fits of panic.
